source.title: Jailbreaking LLMs via Calibration
source.authors: Yuxuan Lu; Yong-Kang Guo; Yuqing Kong

page_placements.theme: Adversarial control extends beyond harmful-request refusal

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether inference-time aggregation of model outputs can bypass refusals on harmful prompts and reports harmful-prompt attack success. This is a different method from fine-tuning or compliant-token prefilling, and it does not measure the per-position KL distribution.
record.gate_note: The harmful-prompt red-team results in Figure 4 test V4 through inference-time logit aggregation and report ASR. Figure values are not numerically labelled in the text, so those rows use figure only. The paper also reports harmfulness scores, but they measure response harmfulness rather than refusal/compliance itself and are not included as V4 rows. The math experiment measures recovery of answers from a target explicitly LoRA-tuned to refuse math; these results concern an induced, non-harmful refusal rather than ordinary safety behavior, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. No fine-tuning-on-harmful-or-benign-data experiment, token-position KL measurement, compliant-opening prefill, suffix attack, or test of why safety is shallow is reported.
record.test_reason: The study reports harmful-prompt attack success rates on HarmBench and StrongREJECT for a decoding-time intervention. It aggregates the target's next-token distribution with an unaligned helper and an aligned predictor, against Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and gpt-oss-120b. That is a decoding change aimed at defeating refusal, so it bears on V4 by a different method. It does no fine-tuning, measures no per-position KL, and does no parameter localization or deepening training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Weak-to-Strong logit arithmetic is a special case of an optimal Gradient Shift aggregation rule, which they prove dominates the target under their assumptions. They find the new hybrid rule the most effective, and the only method that effectively jailbreaks gpt-oss-120b, with near-zero jailbreak tax on math. They state the calibration framing is a modeling choice, not a claim about alignment's mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Builds on Weak-to-Strong inference-time model aggregation and includes it as a baseline, but derives a broader loss-based Gradient Shift family and introduces a hybrid rule; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-position-KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Target model and aggregation rule affect ASR: hybrid performs effectively on gpt-oss-120b, while the other tested methods remain below 30%. The red-team evaluation uses HarmBench and StrongREJECT; figures show results by dataset, but the text does not report separate numerical values by dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Inference-time aggregation recovers math answers from a Llama-3.1-70B model LoRA-tuned to refuse math. Success is 0.99 on GSM8K with hybrid, falling to 0.51 for additive aggregation on MATH level 5. Weak-to-Strong (k=40) is lower than hybrid or multiplicative on harder MATH.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoding-time aggregation can undo an induced, non-safety refusal behaviour with little utility loss. Opening-only steering is less effective on longer, harder tasks.

record.problems: The harmful-prompt ASR values in Figure 4 are not numerically stated in the text. The evaluation uses automated judges; the paper describes HarmBench ASR and StrongREJECT scoring, but reports no uncertainty estimates. Red-team comparisons are limited to the inference-time aggregation family under the shared protocol.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row cap. Harmfulness judge scores in Figures 4 and 6 are not separately rowed because the recorded claim version concerns refusal/compliance, and those scores measure response harmfulness. Other figure-only reference bars (helper, predictor, target) are also not separately rowed.

untested.parts: Not tested: compliant-prefix prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and plain decoding-hyperparameter changes. There is no numeric comparison of opening-only (k=40) versus full-sequence manipulation on Llama-3.3-70B. No ASR as a function of the number of manipulated tokens is reported.
No harmful fine-tuning is done. The helper models are third-party uncensored fine-tunes, but their creation is not studied.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No localization of safety in parameters.
The calibration framing is explicitly a modeling choice and is not tested as a cause.

missing.what: Target-only (no attack) ASR and helper ASR reference bars. These are the baseline every V4 row needs, and they are plotted but not rowed or stated numerically.

Harmfulness scores (StrongREJECT rubric, MD-Judge, HarmScore) per method. The text says hybrid's advantage over Weak-to-Strong persists under these judges, which bears on judge-dependence of the bypass.
missing.locator: Figure 4 lower panels; Appendix C.2, Figure 6

record.verdict_notes: All harmful-prompt ASR values are figure-only, so every state rests on the text's qualitative statements. The attack depends on an unaligned helper sharing the target's tokenizer, and hybrid ASR is bounded by the helper's ASR. The most V4-relevant contrast is opening-only Weak-to-Strong (k=40) failing on gpt-oss-120b while hybrid succeeds, though non-hybrid full-sequence rules also fail there. So the failure cannot be attributed to the opening-only restriction alone. ASR is judged by the HarmBench classifier only, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is performed.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully selected benign data is performed.
No per-token KL comparison of aligned and base models is measured.
Tests inference-time model-output aggregation on harmful prompts. Does not test compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or whether merely passing the first response tokens causes bypass.
No localization of safety to parameters, weights, or ranks.
The proposed calibration account is a modeling abstraction; the study does not test whether data or a training objective causes shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety across response positions, or test of its durability.

tranche.reason: Helper-based next-token aggregation is a different method testing whether decoding interventions elicit harmful compliance, as specified by V4.

source_check.notes: Figure-only ASRs and target baselines cannot be recovered numerically from this text. Math success measures answering regardless of correctness and concerns deliberately induced math refusal, not harmful-request safety.

statements.correction: Section 6: non-hybrid methods on gpt-oss-120b have ASR below 30%; only hybrid is described as effectively jailbreaking this target. Weak-to-Strong modifies the first 40 generated tokens. Verdict: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The below-30% statement is correct, but the challenges label requires an absent or reversed effect; the textual upper bound does not establish that.

statements.correction: Section 5.1 evaluates helper-based aggregation. Appendix C.1 specifies temperature=0.6, no top-k or top-p truncation, and zero frequency and presence penalties. No standalone decoding-hyperparameter bypass sweep is reported.
statements.problem: The absence of a standalone hyperparameter sweep is supported by the experimental scope, but the paper does not explicitly declare that gap.

statements.correction: Figure 4(a): Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Weak-to-Strong alpha=1.0, 1.5, 2.0 with k=40, plus additive, multiplicative and hybrid Gradient Shift. Values are figure only. Section 5.1: alpha=1 and k=infinity makes Weak-to-Strong equivalent to multiplicative aggregation. No same-rule numerical duration ablation is reported.
statements.problem: The paper has no explicit untested-parts declaration. Figure 4(a) includes opening-only Weak-to-Strong results for Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as well as full-sequence aggregation results; these are not confined to GPT-OSS. Exact numerical values and an isolated duration comparison are missing.
